chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from 'Abd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

The ghusl (ritual bath) for janabah, and the ghusl of Friday, the two 'Ids, the Day of 'Arafah, three nights in the month of Ramadan, when you enter the Haram, when you intend to enter the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and for the one who has washed the deceased.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, for which a ghusl is prescribed
key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: the sacred sanctuary whose entry is accompanied by ghusl
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two 'Id festivals, occasions for ghusl
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, during which certain nights are marked for ghusl
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الرَّسُولِ: the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, for whose entry ghusl is performed
key_terms.يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of 'Arafah, a sacred day associated with ghusl

ai.seo_question: On which occasions is ghusl prescribed or recommended in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith lists several occasions for ghusl (ritual bath), including obligatory and recommended instances connected to worship, sacred times, and sacred places. It reflects the importance of taharah (ritual purity) in preparing for acts of devotion and entering honored settings.
